statement: For a finite or countably infinite partition {B_n} of the sample space (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive) and any event A, P(A) = Σ_n P(A|B_n) P(B_n). In the continuous case, for a random variable X with distribution function F_X, P(A) = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} P(A|X=x) dF_X(x), which reduces to P(A) = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} P(A|X=x) f_X(x) dx when X has density f_X.

symbols.meaning: the event whose total probability is sought
n-th event of a mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive partition of the sample space
marginal probability of partition element B_n
conditional probability of A given B_n
continuous random variable used to condition A in the continuous case
density function of X, when it exists

steps.text: Take {B_n : n=1,2,3,...} mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive. Then for any event A, the sets {A ∩ B_n} are disjoint and their union equals A, so summing (marginalizing over the partition index n) gives P(A) = Σ_n P(A ∩ B_n).

By the definition of conditional probability, P(A ∩ B_n) = P(A|B_n) P(B_n) for each n with P(B_n) ≠ 0; if P(B_n) = 0 the term is simply omitted from the summation since P(A|B_n) need not be finite there.
Substituting the result of step 2 into the sum from step 1 yields the law of total probability: P(A) = Σ_n P(A|B_n) P(B_n).

Replacing the discrete partition by conditioning on a continuous random variable X (with distribution function F_X) turns the sum into a Stieltjes integral: P(A) = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} P(A|X=x) dF_X(x). If X admits a density f_X, this specializes to P(A) = ∫_{-∞}^{∞} P(A|X=x) f_X(x) dx, the continuous analogue of marginalizing over n.

assumptions.assumption: {B_n} is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (a true partition of the sample space).
assumptions.breaks_when: The B_n overlap (double-counts probability mass) or fail to cover all outcomes (undercounts probability mass).

assumptions.assumption: Probability is countably additive, so the sum over a countably infinite partition equals P(A).
assumptions.breaks_when: Working in a setting with only finite additivity, where the countable sum need not equal P(A).

assumptions.assumption: In the continuous case, X is a well-defined random variable with distribution function F_X; the simplified integral form additionally requires X to admit a density f_X.
assumptions.breaks_when: X has no density (e.g. a mixed discrete-continuous distribution), in which case only the general dF_X(x) Stieltjes form applies, not f_X(x)dx.

failure_modes.mode: Double-counting or gaps in the partition
failure_modes.signature: Recomputed P(A) disagrees with a direct calculation, or Σ_n P(B_n) ≠ 1.
failure_modes.cause: The chosen B_n are not actually mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.

failure_modes.signature: P(A|B_n) is undefined or ill-posed for some n.
failure_modes.cause: P(B_n) = 0 for that n; per the source, such terms must be omitted from the sum rather than evaluated.

failure_modes.signature: Using P(A) = ∫ P(A|X=x) f_X(x) dx when no density exists.
failure_modes.cause: X does not admit a density function, so the density-based integral is invalid and the general dF_X(x) form must be used instead.

instantiation.why_here: The law of total probability is an underlying mathematical requirement for the recursive state estimation algorithms in ekf_global and ekf_local, as well as the occupancy mapping in obstaclelayer. In the continuous case, the Extended Kalman Filter prediction step (the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation) integrates over the continuous state space using total probability to compute the prior state distribution. The project components depend on this result purely at the algorithmic level for state propagation and sensor fusion, rather than exposing parameters that configure the theorem.

concrete.in_your_project: The continuous 15-dimensional robot state vector at the previous time step in ekf_global and ekf_local, encompassing 3D position, orientation, linear velocity, angular velocity, and linear acceleration.
The probability density function of the 15-dimensional state vector X, represented in the EKF by a multivariate Gaussian distribution N(x̂, P).
The cumulative distribution function of the 15-dimensional continuous robot state vector X.
The event that the robot state at the current time step falls within a specific subset of the 15-dimensional state space, or the event of observing a sensor measurement vector.
The n-th discrete partition state of a costmap grid cell (such as being occupied or free) in obstaclelayer.
The marginal prior probability of a grid cell occupying state B_n in obstaclelayer.
The conditional probability of receiving sensor observation A given that a grid cell is in discrete state B_n in obstaclelayer.
